clue.text: Service stalls appealing to large number of people

definitions.text: appealing to large number of people

parts.note: a Mass is a church service
a market is a collection of traders' stalls

explanation.surface: Church service stalls are drawing crowds of worshippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalls' reads as a verb (delays) but is a noun: the stalls of a market.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods for the mass market are aimed at the broad general public rather than a niche.

clue.text: Tom's troubled but not in the least

definitions.note: read literally: the opposite of 'the least'

indicators.note: troubled suggests something stirred up, so the letters of Tom's are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tom is upset, though not remotely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in the least' normally means 'not at all'; here it is read literally as the opposite of least, its superlative partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of the smallest amount is the greatest amount, so the reverse of least is its antonym.

clue.text: Fly upwards in this way on arrival

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
AR is the abbreviation for arrival, as on timetables

explanation.surface: Instructions to a bird or plane on how to climb when it arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb high through the air is to rise aloft on wings.

clue.text: Way into the sea?

parts.note: read as a door or entry leading into the ocean, using the old poetic word for the sea, rather than a building's principal doorway

explanation.surface: Someone asks where one gets into the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the sea (as in 'the Spanish Main'), so a way into it is wittily a main entrance, the front door of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's principal doorway is its front way in, here punned on 'main' meaning ocean.

clue.text: Reginald and I take on district

parts.note: Reg is the short form of the name Reginald
taken as written, the I taking it on at the end

explanation.surface: Reginald and the speaker agree to take charge of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or zone of a country.

clue.text: Old lawsuit involving exorbitant demand

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
an action is a legal case brought in court

explanation.surface: An old court case concerning an excessive claim for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is an extortionate levy or payment forcibly required of someone.

clue.text: Preserve black sidepiece

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured jam served on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright post forming the side of a doorway or window frame.

clue.text: One regrets being this

parts.note: read as a description of the state of someone saying sorry, not as a confession that one dislikes being something

explanation.surface: Someone wishes they were not a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person who regrets their character; in fact 'one regrets' is a person expressing regret, which is what being sorry looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of regret and saying sorry is contrite and sorry-sounding.

clue.text: Dictatorial authority that's relatively large?

definitions.meaning: the all-watching ruler of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, now any intrusive state power
a family member, a relative, who is big

explanation.surface: A tyrannical government that is fairly big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' reads as 'comparatively', but it means 'as a relative': a sibling who is the larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's surveillance state figure became a byword for an intrusive regime; literally, an older male sibling is a big family member.

clue.text: Resinous substance reportedly hits roof first

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: roof gives ceiling and hits gives whacks, the roof word placed first

explanation.surface: A substance made of resin apparently strikes the top of a room before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the roof word (ceiling) before the hitting word (whacks); 'ceiling whacks' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax is made from shellac and other resins, melted to seal letters.

clue.text: Departing losing single medal

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the word for departing

parts.note: going means leaving or departing
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A competitor leaving without one prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration, as in honours lists.

clue.text: Confiscating band of gold after search in bishop's domain

indicators.note: after puts the band at the end, following the rest
in places the word for search inside the word for bishop's domain

parts.note: a see is the diocese governed by a bishop
a quest is a search
a ring is a band of gold

explanation.surface: Seizing a gold ring once it has been hunted for in the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequestering assets means legally seizing or impounding them, especially until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Opener major receives

definitions.meaning: what a person reaching legal majority traditionally gets

explanation.surface: A leading opener is given something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like an adjective (the chief opener) but is a noun: someone who has come of age. The key of the door was the traditional symbolic gift on turning 21.
explanation.definitionFit: A house key literally opens the entrance; giving one marked coming of age, the age of majority.

clue.text: Drunk on horseback

parts.note: read as a drink taken while mounted, rather than an intoxicated rider

explanation.surface: An inebriated rider in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective describing a rider but is a past participle: something drunk, a drink. A stirrup cup is the drink served to riders mounted before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders traditionally take a farewell toast in the saddle before setting off, especially in fox hunting.

clue.text: Go first, have quick look at grey mineral

parts.note: to lead is to go in front
to glance is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Advice to take the lead and briefly inspect a grey rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead glance is an old name for galena, the grey lead sulphide ore.

clue.text: Score went in the oriental heard

indicators.note: heard means the built letters are taken by their spoken sound

parts.note: went goes inside T plus E: 'the' shortened to T as in dialect t', and oriental giving E for eastern

explanation.surface: Score of a match that went into an Asian contest, as overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' becomes T (the dialect t') and 'oriental' gives E (east); 'in' puts WENT inside them for T-WENT-E, which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

clue.text: Put on record

parts.note: read as placing a song on a disc, but meaning to write something down officially

explanation.surface: Instruction to place something on a vinyl disc.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb also has a noun sense, a paper or record itself, so the clue works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down in writing as evidence is to register it formally.

clue.text: Country nawab's to reorganise

indicators.note: reorganise asks for the letters of nawab's and to to be rearranged into a new order

parts.note: nawab's minus the apostrophe gives the letters NAWABS

explanation.surface: An Indian governor's realm is to be restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa.

clue.text: Warmer in the house perhaps

parts.note: read as a comparison of temperatures indoors, but meaning a device that heats a home

explanation.surface: A remark that it may be warmer indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: a thing that warms, such as a domestic heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic heater circulating hot water to heat rooms is a typical household warming device.

clue.text: So grieves audibly at the trial

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase built is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: so gives as, and grieves gives sighs

explanation.surface: Someone groans so much during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Assizes were periodic county courts in England and Wales until 1972; one sitting was an assize, so the word can mean a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a court session or the trial held at one, in old English law.

clue.text: State gold was found in swampy ground

indicators.note: was found in places the word for gold inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Mass is the abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A US state where gold was discovered in marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or marsh.

clue.text: Not a good-looking one to serve

definitions.text: Not a good-looking one to serve

parts.words: Not a good-looking one to serve
parts.note: read literally as an unattractive shop patron, but meaning a nasty, menacing person

explanation.surface: A shop assistant faced with an unattractive patron.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means an unpleasant, dangerous person; the clue reads it literally as a plain-looking patron waiting to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a threatening or difficult individual, literally an unattractive patron in a shop.

clue.text: Rival went initially to watch

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to rival

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of went

explanation.surface: A competitor set off first to observe.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to look at or observe it.

clue.text: Part of poem mysteriously receives award

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of an enigmatic poem wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'receives award' as the definition, but the answer is a noun and cannot mean 'receives award'; 'receives' only links the hidden run to the award it names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the US television industry's annual prize, a statuette.

clue.text: Small creature found source of water not in Welsh town

indicators.note: not in says that letter is taken out of the town's name

parts.note: Conwy is a walled town in north Wales

indicators.note: source of means just the opening letter of water is wanted

explanation.surface: A little animal discovered a spring missing from a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: CONWY loses its W to leave the answer, an old word for a rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cony is a rabbit, or in the Bible the rock hyrax, a small mammal.

clue.text: Can a misfit develop excessive enthusiasm?

indicators.note: develop suggests changing into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether an oddball might become a zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanaticism is extreme, obsessive zeal for a cause.

clue.text: Pair you brought back of hunted animals

indicators.note: brought back means the old word for you is turned round

parts.note: ye is the old word for you

explanation.surface: A couple you have returned with, of animals chased by hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey are the creatures that predators chase and kill for food.

clue.text: Spend time in characteristic manner in corridor

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a period of time
a way is someone's typical manner of doing things

explanation.surface: Whiling away the hours in one's usual fashion in a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A passageway is a narrow way through a building, a hall or corridor.
